tweets.text: How it started:                 How it's going:

a big problem in our industry

you have simplified frameworks

meanwhile, how actual successful teams work is messy

companies adopt the simple frameworks and then apply their legacy process to the new way to fill in the gaps

we don't talk enough about operationalizing things

change agent tip

you are likely spending 10x more time thinking about X than the person you are trying to influence

there is no way they'll have bandwidth to process your 10x.

you have to impedance match

Me: "It's fractal and messy"

Amazing. @misaelneto combined ideas from myself, @cagan, @herbigt, @slidbook, @gibsonbiddle, @sebastienphl,

a PRD - product requirements document

comes after:
* a vision
* a strategy
* A North Star Metric and Inputs
* detailed core beliefs/ ssumptions
* open-ended research
* bet 1-pager(s)
* persona-ish things
* detailed history of prior bets
* learning backlog
* (10 other things)
Good thing this never happens in product.

Here is where most "product transformations" in the enterprise are getting stuck.

The messy middle.

Not "Agile".

An actual "digital" strategy (that has a unique perspective on how to use design, data, technology to achieve business goals)

keep in mind that if your role involves being an "integrator" across multiple teams ... and you don't manage people directly ... there's a good chance you have a view of your org that no one (even the CEO) has ...

and you're taking on an emotional burden most ppl don't take on

if you don't slow down to speed up

you'll be forced to slow down

and it will not be on your terms

happens with people

happens with companies ... they hit the wall and have to "rebuild"

I am a big believer in teams having a *suitably detailed* one year-ish rolling roadmap at the ready.

The trick? Suitably detailed.

Think of it as progressively disclosing options/solutions.
